sources.title: Genome of Bacteriophage P1 (2004)
sources.supports: Opened primary genome paper: P1 lysogenizes as a low-copy plasmid and supports generalized transduction; tail is a tube surrounded by a contractile sheath with six fibers.

sources.title: Visualization of bacteriophage P1 infection by cryo-electron tomography of tiny Escherichia coli (2011)
sources.supports: Opened primary abstract and figure captions: contractile P1 tail tube penetrates the outer envelope into periplasm. The paper leaves aspects of inner-membrane DNA entry unresolved; no claim is made here that P1 must literally pierce the inner membrane.

sources.title: Structural mechanism of bacteriophage lambda tail’s interaction with the bacterial receptor (2024)
sources.supports: Opened primary PDF: LamB interaction opens the central tail apparatus; DNA passage needs a trans-envelope route. The paper distinguishes LamB recognition from passage through its small maltose pore, and leaves parts of trans-envelope architecture uncertain.

findings.location: tail shaft construction 170-177; update 267-292; envelopeDetail.js rodCutaway 4-77
findings.evidence: During injection at p=0.8, both branches have tube-tip world position [2.65,1.04,0], while actual recipient triangle ray intersections are y=0.9 and y=0.8325. The tube stops 0.14 above the outer surface. DNA crosses the intact cutaway envelope at the same axis; no receptor/trans-envelope aperture or connecting conduit is drawn. See evidence/genome/diagnostics.json (p=0.8).
findings.whyWrong: The displayed transfer is through the bare envelope after leaving a disconnected tail. P1 must engage and penetrate the outer envelope; lambda requires an attached receptor-triggered entry apparatus. Exact inner-membrane molecular composition need not be invented to preserve a continuous schematic route.
findings.fix: Join each route’s tail/entry apparatus to an explicit recipient entry opening before injection. Provide a bounded schematic trans-envelope conduit consistent with P1 vs lambda morphology; open only that envelope region and preserve the cutaway, DNA continuity and cargo identity. Do not assert that the ordinary LamB maltose pore itself passes DNA.
findings.verification: At sampled injection states for both roots and routes, actual transformed cargo endpoints traverse a connected tail-to-envelope route, recipient membrane triangles do not intersect the cargo path outside the intended entry opening, and DNA reaches cytoplasm while capsid stays outside. Repeated arbitrary seeks retain resources.

findings.evidence: At p=0.23 the donor locus disappears by a binary present() test and a separate straight cargo contour appears at another pose. The computed extract=ease(p,0.16,0.33) is unused. Across 0.23 +/- 1e-7, every donor gold rail-center sample has a positive distance to the nearest gold cargo segment center: P1 min/mean/max 0.194/0.439/0.610, lambda 0.484/0.591/0.694 world units (evidence/genome/continuity.json).
findings.whyWrong: The highlighted material the user is tracking switches directly from a donor chromosomal arc to a spatially separated straight line; this is an object handoff jump, not nucleotide-scale growth or a biologically intentional pause. The model explicitly teaches movement from donor locus into transferred cargo.
findings.fix: Use one continuous, identity-preserving extraction-to-packaging path. Start transferred cargo on the donor locus, detach/morph continuously over the extraction interval, and hand off between contour representations only at matching positions without duplicated donor DNA.
findings.verification: Dense samples around extraction start/end and the former 0.23 threshold must have no finite displacement as delta-progress tends to zero; ensure the donor locus and cargo are neither both present as duplicated substrate nor simultaneously absent. Check P1 and lambda color identity and world-space contour continuity.

checked: Cargo path branches meet at u=0 and u=-0.22; this part of injection is spatially continuous.

sources.title: FisB mediates membrane fission during sporulation in Bacillus subtilis (2013)
sources.supports: Opened primary paper PDF: polar septation, membrane migration around forespore, final neck fission; SpoIIIE moves chromosome into the forespore. Used for staged topology and translocase interpretation.

sources.title: Ultrastructure of macromolecular assemblies contributing to bacterial spore resistance revealed by in situ cryo-electron tomography (2024)
sources.supports: Opened primary cryo-ET paper PDF, pp. 1-2: cortex is synthesized in intermembrane space; coat assembles on the surface of the outer forespore membrane. Observed cutaways must preserve that radial order.

findings.evidence: Mature inner/outer membrane rear radii are 0.72/0.87, but cortex/coat rear surfaces are at 0.70/0.85. Actual triangle ray intersections at p=1 from spore center along -z are inner 0.72000003, cortex 0.70000000, outer 0.87000000, coat 0.85000000. 47/1025 cortex vertices lie inside the inner ellipsoid and 41/1025 coat vertices lie inside the outer ellipsoid. At p=0.58 the cortex rear is already only 0.594 while inner membrane remains 0.72. See evidence/genome/diagnostics.json and continuity.json.
findings.whyWrong: The labeled cortex must lie between the forespore membranes and the coat outside the outer membrane. Different y/z aspect ratios cause actual surface crossing on the retained rear half of the cutaway, reversing radial order; this is not a camera-only occlusion or nearest-vertex proxy.
findings.fix: Derive all visible membrane, cortex, coat shells and edge details from compatible nested profiles throughout maturation. Keep the cortex outside the inner membrane and inside the outer membrane at every visible point; keep coat outside the outer membrane. Preserve continuous engulfment attachment and existing layer detail.
findings.verification: Actual transformed triangle or analytic surface containment/ray-order checks for multiple rear directions across p=0.57..1, plus arbitrary seeks and the blocked branch. Require inner < cortex < outer < coat with positive clearance whenever each is visible; old chromosome/translocase/engulfment invariants must remain passing.

checked: All formation, wrap, maturation and release intervals, especially 0.13/0.24/0.32/0.43/0.56/0.57/0.63/0.89/0.92/0.93.
